# Proposal: Practitioner Academy for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Source:** Client Profile Block v1.0, drawn from discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Profile Block records three AI use cases:

* a deployed customer service chatbot on the support portal
* an AI visual inspection pilot on the German production line
* AI sales forecasting planned for next year

AI maturity is recorded as Piloting. Regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned to start next year, with the start date not fixed.

RISK_EVENTS records an internal audit finding of June 2026: no inventory of AI systems.

Your stated objective, Dana Whitfield, is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why Practitioner Capability Fits Now

Two facts point to the same need: a recorded finding of no AI system inventory and a stated objective tied to a production date. Both call for working artifacts built by the people named in AUDIENCE_ROLES:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* two internal auditors

The Practitioner Academy is built for that work. Participants work directly in two open repositories:

* the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Each person leaves with artifacts started and knows where every instrument lives. The program applies three principles throughout: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

INCUMBENT_FRAMEWORKS lists:

* an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS
* an ISO 9001 quality management system
* an internal audit function

The program will ask at intake which existing records participants may reference. It will not assume any of them exist in a given form. The program does not promise any certification or audit outcome.

## 3. Running Worked Examples

We propose two running examples across both days, with a third used on Day 1 only.

1. **AI visual inspection (piloting).** This is the use case named in your stated objective and its Q2 2027 production date. It gives the program a real deadline to govern against.
2. **Customer service chatbot (deployed).** This is the only deployed system in the Profile Block. The stated constraint that customer data must stay in the EU makes it the natural case for governed prompting and evidence work.
3. **AI sales forecasting (planned).** Used in Day 1 inventory and classification so the started inventory covers planned as well as live systems.

Every exercise uses a sanitized analog. No customer data or production data enters the sessions or the repositories. The German works council is to be consulted before anything touches production staff. Visual inspection artifacts are therefore produced as drafts for internal review and are not put into use during the program.

## 4. Curriculum Spine

The program runs over two days, live and virtual, with four 90-minute working sessions each day.

| Session | Exercise | Repository asset | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Day 1, S1:** Doctrine and governance structures | *The Turtle and the Phoenix* is told from the facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). The kit's handle map bridges into a roles and decision rights draft for the visual inspection pilot, using AUDIENCE_ROLES titles. The session closes with the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise. | Facilitation kit: story, handle map, section 8 closing exercise. GRC Workbook: governance structures module. | Three artifacts specified in section 8 of the kit. Draft roles and decision rights chart. |
| **Day 1, S2:** Inventory and classification | Enter all three use cases into an inventory and propose a classification for each under the EU AI Act, marked as draft for legal review. | GRC Workbook: AI system inventory and classification module | Started AI system inventory (three entries) |
| **Day 1, S3:** Risk and impact assessments | Assess the visual inspection pilot and the chatbot. The chatbot assessment records the EU data residency constraint as a requirement. | GRC Workbook: risk and impact assessment module | Draft risk register entries for two systems |
| **Day 1, S4:** Policies and operating procedures | Draft an operating procedure for adding a system to the inventory. Draft a policy outline covering the three use cases. | GRC Workbook: policies and operating procedures module | Draft inventory procedure and policy outline |
| **Day 2, S5:** Governed prompting | Build governed prompts for a sanitized analog of chatbot support queries. | Slow AI Kitchen: governed prompting pattern | Governed prompt set with stated intent and limits |
| **Day 2, S6:** Practical AI workflow design | Design two workflows: the chatbot response workflow and a visual inspection defect disposition workflow, using sanitized analogs. | Slow AI Kitchen: practical AI workflow design pattern | Two governed workflow drafts |
| **Day 2, S7:** Human oversight and accountability | Place named human checkpoints in both workflows. Set acceptance criteria for each workflow using The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done). | Slow AI Kitchen: human oversight pattern. GRC Workbook: accountability sections. | Oversight checkpoint map and acceptance criteria |
| **Day 2, S8:** Evidence and audit readiness | Internal auditors lead the build of an evidence index for both workflows. The group drafts a one-page summary shaped by AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). | GRC Workbook: evidence collection and audit readiness module | Evidence index and board-layer summary draft |

Exact file paths for each module and pattern will be supplied in the pre-work packet.

## 5. Deliverables

By the close of Day 2, participants will have started:

* an AI system inventory with three entries
* draft risk register entries for the visual inspection pilot and the chatbot
* at least two governed workflows with oversight checkpoints and acceptance criteria
* the three artifacts produced by the facilitation kit's section 8 closing exercise
* supporting drafts: a roles chart, a procedure, a policy outline, a prompt set, an evidence index and a summary

All of these are starting artifacts for the Client to complete. They are not finished governance.

## 6. Logistics and Price

* **Format:** two days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day
* **Price:** US$12,500
* **Budget context:** the Profile Block records budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year
* **Dates and session time zone:** Unknown, to be set at intake

## 7. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. Which participants attend each session, and in which time zone should sessions run?
2. Does the German works council need to be consulted on the visual inspection exercise drafts, even as sanitized analogs?
3. May participants work in public repository forks, or does the Client require private copies?
4. Which existing ISMS, quality or audit records, if any, may be referenced in the exercises?
5. Who will own finishing each artifact after the program?

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 30-minute intake call with you, Dana Whitfield, to confirm the questions above and fix dates.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: S7 lists 'GRC Workbook: accountability sections' and the Definition of Done appears in the exercise text rather than the asset column. I read this as naming the repository asset adequately. A stricter scorer could call it vague and fail item 4.

'Internal auditors lead the build of an evidence index' in S8 assigns a role. I treated it as proposed work using AUDIENCE_ROLES, which scorer guidance v1.14.3 allows, not as an asserted Client fact or relation. Another scorer could read it as an inferred relation under Guardrail 6.
The proposal may run past two pages. The checklist does not score length, so I did not treat it as a failure.
I treated 'Source: ... drawn from discovery call notes of 6 October 2026' as a restatement of SOURCE_MATERIAL, not a new fact.
